title: U.S. House · Missouri's 7th District
area: Southwest Missouri, including Springfield and Joplin.

context.text: Incumbent Eric Burlison won the August 4, 2026 Republican primary over John Casey and Grayson Hunt. Missi Hesketh ran unopposed in the Democratic primary. Kevin Craig advanced unopposed in the Libertarian primary.

candidates.name: Eric Burlison

summary.text: Eric Burlison is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Missouri's 7th District, first elected in 2022. A sixth-generation Missourian, he worked about 20 years as an investment advisor and software consultant before serving in the Missouri House and Senate. He serves on the House Oversight and Government Reform and Transportation and Infrastructure committees.

background.text: Born in Springfield, Missouri, and, according to his congressional website, a sixth-generation Missourian.
Graduated from Parkview High School in Springfield in 1995, then earned a Bachelor of Arts in Philosophy and a Master of Business Administration from Missouri State University.
According to his congressional website, had 20 years of private-sector experience as an investment advisor and software consultant.
Represented District 133 in the Missouri House of Representatives from 2009 to 2017.
Won election to the Missouri Senate in 2018 and represented the 20th Senatorial District (Christian County and part of Greene County) from 2019 to 2023.

Won the open 7th District U.S. House seat in November 2022, defeating Democrat Kristen Radaker-Sheafer, Libertarian Kevin Craig and a write-in candidate, and took office in 2023; succeeded Billy Long.

Serves on the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, where he chairs the Subcommittee on Economic Growth, Energy Policy, and Regulatory Affairs and sits on the Subcommittee on Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), and on the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure (Highways and Transit; Railroads, Pipelines, and Hazardous Materials; Water Resources and Environment).
Held a hearing on state and local natural gas bans as chair of his Oversight subcommittee, and co-launched an Oversight investigation into Bloomberg Philanthropies funding.
Won the August 4, 2026 Republican primary with 73.8% of the vote over Grayson Hunt and John Casey.
According to his congressional website, he and his wife Angie live in Ozark, Missouri, with their two daughters.

priorities.text: As chairman of the Economic Growth, Energy Policy, and Regulatory Affairs subcommittee, has focused on opposing state and local bans on natural gas, arguing they raise energy costs for households.

positions.summary: Opposes state and local government bans on natural gas and other fossil fuels intended to speed a shift to electrification, and is investigating philanthropic funding of anti-fossil-fuel advocacy groups.
positions.quote: Over the last several years, the Biden Administration and Congressional Democrats sought to force Americans away from natural gas and other fossil fuels and towards electrification.

record.text: Served on the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure, and the Committee on Education and the Workforce during the 2023-2024 session (118th Congress).

candidates.researchNotes: Burlison has not completed a 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey. His official House issues page has no topic subpages with stated-position text; recent press releases include one directly addressing the pace of the transition away from fossil fuels (opposing state/local natural gas bans), used above. candidates.name: Missi Hesketh
candidates.ballotNote: Ran unopposed in the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary

summary.text: Missi Hesketh is the Democratic nominee for Missouri's 7th District and a former alderwoman and mayor of Forsyth, Missouri. She worked in food service, clerical and finance jobs before a career in education. She is campaigning on ending division and restoring accountability and "decency and decorum" to Congress.

background.text: Born in Elmhurst, Illinois, in 1971 according to her Ballotpedia survey; moved to Forsyth, Missouri, with her family in 1983 and graduated from Forsyth High School in 1990.

Describes herself as having attended the University of Missouri for one semester before working in food service, clerical and finance jobs, and says a post-9/11 job change steered her toward education.

Earned a bachelor's degree in elementary education from the University of Missouri-St. Louis (2004), a graduate degree from Drury University (2018) and an Ed.S. from Missouri State University (2023); her survey lists an A.A. in business administration and degrees in elementary, gifted, and special education and assessment.
Has worked as an educator.
Served the city of Forsyth as alderwoman and later as mayor, focusing on recreation and ecotourism, communications and transparency, and enforcement against nuisance and dangerous buildings.
Was the Democratic nominee for this seat in 2024, losing to Burlison 71.6% to 26.3%; she won the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary unopposed.
Describes herself as a single parent of three.

priorities.text: Says she wants to "end the division" in Congress and restore transparency, honesty and integrity, holding public town halls and representing all constituents regardless of party.
Healthcare: says the healthcare system is broken and calls for caps on services, prescriptions and premiums.
Social Security: wants to ensure Social Security stays solvent so future retirees do not face benefit cuts.

positions.summary: Says she wants to "codify Roe" and give women and their partners autonomy over reproductive decisions.
Calls for caps on healthcare services, prescriptions and premiums, saying the current system is broken.
Says protecting water, air and soil is essential to the region's ecotourism and farming industries.

candidates.researchNotes: No prior federal or state-level elected office; positions drawn from her 2025 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey. Her survey response included an unverified allegation about the incumbent's vote on a discharge petition, which is omitted here because it was not independently confirmed via a reputable news source.

candidates.name: Kevin Craig
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced unopposed in the August 4, 2026 Libertarian primary

summary.text: Kevin Craig is the Libertarian Party nominee for Missouri's 7th District, a seat he has sought several times. His Ballotpedia profile lists a career as a writer and editor and a law degree.

background.text: Earned a high school diploma from Lowell High School, a bachelor's degree from the University of Southern California (1979) and a law degree from Trinity Law School (1984).
Career experience listed as a writer and an editor.
Was the Libertarian candidate for Missouri's 7th District in 2012 (5.2%), 2014 (7.7%), 2020 (4.2%), 2022 (2.3%) and 2024 (2.2%), each time finishing third.

candidates.researchNotes: Ballotpedia notes Craig completed a Candidate Connection survey, but it was not reachable in this research pass; no other public statements of positions were confirmed.
